products.overview: Four wavelengths at full intensity, at once. The original managed one. Running multiple light wavelengths together used to mean turning the intensity down. PhotoCube Plus doesn't make that trade. It runs four wavelengths simultaneously, at full intensity, where the original PhotoCube could only manage one before intensity had to drop. Any commercially available wavelength from 257 to 650 nm is usable, not a fixed set. An optional cooler module holds vials at 10–15°C at maximum LED power; without it, that same power runs at 40–50°C. The choice is real and it matters for reaction control. It's the first ThalesNano system built for both batch and flow. Four vials in batch mode, or an 8 mL loop in continuous flow, at 0.1 to 10 mL/min, on the same device.
features: Four Simultaneous Wavelengths, Full Intensity: Runs together without the intensity trade-off the original PhotoCube required.
Open Wavelength Range: Any commercially available wavelength from 257 to 650 nm, with custom types available on request.
Automatic Safety Shutdown: Lighting shuts off immediately when the device door opens.
Optional Cooler Module: Cold finger technology holds vials at 10–15°C at maximum LED power, versus 40–50°C without it.
Batch and Flow Operation: Runs vial-based batch reactions or continuous flow chemistry on the same device.
Touchscreen Light Intensity Control: Direct, seamless adjustment of light intensity per wavelength.
THS ReAction Software Compatible: Supports in-line analytics and both manual and automated remote control.
24 W Per Color Light Capacity: A specific, confirmed maximum power figure per wavelength.

faqs.question: What is the PhotoCube™ Plus used for?
faqs.answer: It's an LED photochemistry reactor used for reactions including bromination, C-C coupling, the Minisci reaction, and thiol-ene click chemistry, in both batch and continuous flow.

faqs.question: How many wavelengths can run at once?
faqs.answer: Up to four, at full intensity, a genuine improvement over the original PhotoCube's limit of one wavelength at high intensity.

faqs.question: How do I choose between batch and flow mode?
faqs.answer: Use batch mode with 4x4 mL or 4x30 mL vials for screening and method development, or flow mode with an 8 mL loop at 0.1 to 10 mL/min for continuous, scaled-up production.

faqs.question: How do I set up cooling for a temperature-sensitive reaction?
faqs.answer: Add the optional cooler module, which uses cold finger technology to hold vials at 10 to 15°C at maximum LED power, compared to 40 to 50°C without it.

faqs.question: What wavelength range is available?
faqs.answer: Any commercially available wavelength from 257 to 650 nm, with a basic configuration of 365, 457, 523, and 625 nm, and custom wavelengths available on request.

faqs.question: Is the PhotoCube Plus safe to open while running?
faqs.answer: Yes. Opening the device door triggers an automatic lighting shutdown.

faqs.question: What pumps are compatible with the PhotoCube Plus?
faqs.answer: Knauer HPLC pumps (10 or 50 mL/min) and Eldex Optos HPLC pumps (up to 80 mL/min) are both confirmed compatible.

faqs.question: Can the PhotoCube Plus connect to ThalesNano's fleet system?
faqs.answer: Yes, through the THS System Controller and THS RS232-CAN Converter, using THS ReAction Software for remote and automated control.

faqs.question: What is the difference between PhotoCube Plus and the original PhotoCube?
faqs.answer: PhotoCube Plus runs four wavelengths at full intensity simultaneously versus the original's one, covers an open 257-650 nm range instead of a fixed set, and adds a proper cooler module and fleet compatibility the original didn't have.

faqs.question: What is the price of the PhotoCube™ Plus in India?
faqs.answer: The price depends on whether you include the cooler module and any custom wavelength requirements. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your application is confirmed.

faqs.question: Who is the authorized distributor of the PhotoCube™ Plus in India?
faqs.answer: Inkarp is the authorized distributor and service provider for the ThalesNano PhotoCube™ Plus in India, providing demonstration, installation, training, AMC, spare parts, and technical support.

sections.title: PhotoCube™ Plus at a Glance
sections.subheading: Why running 4 wavelengths at full intensity is a real generational leap
sections.description: Everything you need to evaluate PhotoCube Plus: how multi-wavelength control and cooling actually work, how batch and flow modes differ, which reactions it supports, and Inkarp installation and service support.
body: Simultaneous wavelengths no longer mean a lower ceiling. Four wavelengths run together at full intensity, where the original PhotoCube limited simultaneous use to one wavelength at high intensity.
The wavelength range is genuinely open, not a fixed menu. Any commercially available wavelength from 257 to 650 nm, not the original's set list of specific values.
Cooling changes the reaction temperature dramatically. 10–15°C with the cooler module, versus 40–50°C without it, at the same maximum LED power.
Safety shuts the light off automatically. Opening the device door triggers an immediate lighting shutdown.
It runs both batch and flow, genuinely. Vials with magnetic stirring for batch work, or a loop for continuous flow, on the same unit.
The interface moved onto the device itself. A real usability change from the original PhotoCube's external interface.

Module compatibility is narrower than the hydrogenation product lines. Confirmed compatible with Knauer and Eldex Optos HPLC pumps and ThalesNano's fleet controllers — not the broader H-Genie/Phoenix module ecosystem.

Confirmed solution: ThalesNano PhotoCube™ Plus. Light source: LED, up to 4 wavelengths simultaneously, 257-650 nm range. Basic configuration: 365, 457, 523, 625 nm (custom wavelengths on request). Operating modes: batch (vials) and flow (loop). Full application-specific wavelength recommendations are available on request from Inkarp.
Tell our team your target reaction and whether you need batch or flow operation, and Inkarp will confirm the right wavelength and cooling configuration.

sections.title: What the cooler module actually changes
body: Running photochemistry at real intensity, across multiple wavelengths, generates real heat, and that's exactly what the cooler module is built to manage. At maximum LED power, an uncooled vial sits at 40 to 50°C. With the cooler module's cold finger technology engaged, the same power holds the vial at 10 to 15°C, a genuinely different reaction environment for temperature-sensitive photochemistry. Wavelength control runs independently of that, with up to four wavelengths operable at once, at full intensity, across the open 257–650 nm range.
sections.disclaimer: Tell our team your target wavelength(s) and temperature sensitivity, and Inkarp will confirm whether the cooler module is worth including.
